sentences.text: One of history's oldest signatures was a stone smaller than your thumb.
But how do you sign wet clay?
You carve a tiny picture into stone.
But one press makes one mark.
So you roll it, and the picture stands out raised.
But what about a tablet sealed inside an envelope?
You roll the stone across the envelope as well.
This one, at the Met, is about five thousand years old.
And it's still smaller than your thumb.
